backbone: Assuming G rational makes Taylor-contact determinants Delta_N rational; nonvanishing plus p-adic valuation lower bounds and real-place upper estimates are incompatible, so G is irrational.
quote: This agreement cancels the $\zeta(2)$ term in every entry. Consequently, the single hypothesis $G\in\mathbb Q$ makes all the determinants rational.

backbone: Assume arbitrarily good rational approximations to pi; a separated-weight interpolation theorem yields a nonzero determinant whose arithmetic lower bound and analytic upper bound are incompatible.

backbone: Hooley index-divisor reduction: sieve produces many primes with controlled predecessors, and a new Hecke zero-free region bounds Kummer complete-splitting obstructions, leaving c x/(log x)^2 primes with primitive root a.
quote: A large divisor forces $p$ to divide one of a short list of integers $a^j-1$; the remaining divisors are controlled by complete splitting in Kummer fields.

backbone: Build a monodromy-tracked degeneration, construct a special Lagrangian torus from collapsing Ricci-flat metrics, hyperkahler-rotate to a holomorphic Lagrangian torus making e semiample, then deform back via Soldatenkov-Verbitsky.
quote: The proof produces a semiample deformation of $e$ and then returns to $X$.

backbone: Suppose a very general cubic of large discriminant were rational; a divisorial cocycle counting K3-type divisors under weak factorization is evaluated two incompatible ways, forcing a contradiction.
quote: Suppose such an \(X\) were rational, and choose a birational map \(f:\mathbf P^4\dashrightarrow X\).

backbone: For Picard number one, characterization theorems leave pseudoindices four and five; each is excluded or recognized as a Grassmannian via minimal-rational-curve characteristic-class identities certified by exact computation.
quote: Standard characterization theorems leave pseudoindices four and five; the other possibilities are excluded or give projective space $\mathbb P^6$ and the smooth quadric $Q^6$.

backbone: Reduce a.e. convergence to a maximal estimate, proved by induction on scales via a uniform dyadic packet-distribution estimate using transverse, sparse and lossless bilinear savings.
quote: We will obtain a broad bound with constant depending on $K$ and a narrow contraction with a constant independent of $K$. We then choose $K$, the base scale, and the induction constant in that order.

backbone: Upper bound: Gaussian sections plus a randomly sampled hierarchy of folded Gaussian lattice blocks give density Cn log n; lower bound: a random symmetric body defeats all periodic coverings.
quote: A second moment estimate alone gives a good approximation at most base points. A second group of random shifts upgrades this to a lower bound at \emph{every} base point.

backbone: Explicit deterministic algorithm: winners are boundary labels of a clipped potential fixed point, computed by a recursive pivot-and-narrow-box labeling procedure with quasipolynomially many calls.
quote: There is a terminating deterministic procedure $\cL(A,D,a,b)$, using exact evaluations of $\lfloor F(t)\rfloor$ for $t\in\Z^n$ and integer and rational arithmetic, with the following guarantee.

backbone: Explicit matrix tuple: formulas become word-series shift (or differential) systems, an order-of-vanishing bound via Wronskian-type determinants limits truncation, and truncated generic matrices descend to prime-field hitting points.
quote: We construct a single matrix substitution that detects every nonzero size-s division-free noncommutative formula in n variables over every field of a given positive characteristic.

backbone: A small complement automaton yields an order-reversing surjection from a path-diagram monoid onto the relation monoid; induction on h with conjugate amplification of one added pair forces exponentially many states.
quote: We induct on $h$, simultaneously over all the data in the statement, including $m$, $e$, $S$, and $\phi$.

backbone: Reductions turn an existential-universal sentence into two existential tests on implicitly controlled polynomial families, decided by trace/residue determinants, root labels and CRT sign recovery in fixed counting-hierarchy level.
quote: We retain instead three pieces of information: a degree bound, a coefficient-norm bound, and a procedure for evaluation modulo a prime.

backbone: Algebraic unit clusters near lambda force singularity; conversely singularity gives many close cross-pairs of bit words, whose difference vectors are completed to irreducible height-one polynomials with roots just above lambda.
quote: The main step behind the criterion is a realization lemma. Concentration of the measure produces many pairs of finite bit words with nearby sums and different first bits.

backbone: In a least failing dimension, select interpolable directions by excluding sparse cones via polynomial scale profiles, convert equal distances to skew-form flat incidences, and contradict concentration bounds.
quote: Suppose that Theorem~\ref{thm:main} fails, and take the least dimension \(d\ge3\) in which it fails.

backbone: A deterministic staged stub-pairing algorithm (early pairing, cleanup, completion, exact spectral repair by biased switches) is shown via resolvent, trace and moment estimates to output a nonbipartite Ramanujan graph.
quote: For every fixed integer d ≥ 3, we give a deterministic algorithm that constructs a simple nonbipartite d-regular Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices.

backbone: Explicit 66x66 pattern (64x64 anchor plus 2x2 body) and explicit tree-structured hosts: any few changes leave a copy, while all copies are confined to diagonal leaf cells.
quote: We construct a fixed $66\times66$ binary matrix for which ordered matrix removal has no polynomial bound.

backbone: Chain inversion and central-trace calculations reduce l(B)=|W_p(B)| to p-power divisibility of genus-one generating-tuple counts, proved by showing a small Galois orbit of covers contradicts an exact inseparable genus estimate.
quote: Our proof instead passes from a direct block-algebra calculation to covers of curves; it does not use a classification of finite simple groups or an inductive weight condition.

backbone: After a unimodular reduction, amplified endpoint maps give critical moment bounds, then a subpower triangle bound, and corridor deformation gives a spectral contradiction bounding the critical operator norm.
quote: A finite-exploration comparison with critical percolation then contradicts the assumed divergent moment.

backbone: Transfer-matrix particle estimates bound slab crossings, giving tightness of loop curves; subsequential limits are identified with nested CLE4 via cited puncture convergence and exclusion of invisible paths.

backbone: Conditional-flow energy contraction makes ordered marginals of most 7n/8-card lists nearly uniform; an eight-block Fourier lift transfers this to the full permutation; support counting gives the lower bound.
quote: We prove explicitly the dimension estimate and the passage from marginals to the full group law that the argument requires.

backbone: Construct a finitely presented algebra with a simple subalgebra, build a finitely presented envelope with a faithful two-transitive action, then embed into a simple group via cited constructions.
quote: Over \(k=\F_2\), we construct a finitely presented algebra \(B\), a simple subalgebra \(A\subseteq B\) with its own identity, and an injective nonunital map \(\phi:B\to B\) with image in \(A\).

backbone: Finite-interval action method: trial eigenfunctions, a matrix path with prescribed endpoints and an integrated trace comparison bound eigenvalue moments sharply; retained defects force fixed-channel sech^2 equality cases.
quote: The action subtracts a power of the matrix density $\rho(x)=A(x)A(x)^{\mathsf T}$, and a complementary lower bound recovers the sum of the chosen eigenvalue moments.

backbone: Prove localization of conjugated product projections by a finite backward induction over mismatch thresholds, using Chebyshev-type polynomial approximations and depth reduction; localization then bounds the output's parity advantage.
quote: A finite chain of thresholds ends above the maximum possible count $N$, where localization is automatic; working backward proves the original statement (\Cref{sec:bootstrap}).

backbone: From a bifinite correspondence build finite-module boundary measurements over local-field buildings; obstruction and gap-growth arguments force sharp links that glue into finite-index subgroup isomorphisms.
quote: For lattice groups, we prove that this analytic relation comes from a finite collection of actual subgroup isomorphisms.

backbone: Construct a tuple with sparse higher cumulants; after semicircular noise a cumulant Fisher bound keeps chi* near semicircular while persistent microstate block structure forces a deficit in chi.
quote: Here we construct a strict gap with both entropies finite.

backbone: A minimal-order counterexample has a Lie-type component in a short list; for each family, frame cycles, dimension estimates and propagation produce nonzero rational homology, a contradiction.
quote: Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} for $p=2$.

backbone: Assume a positive maximal radial defect; attain it via ultrapowers, align extremal chords by common supports and Darbo's fixed point, and contradict support and convexity estimates.
quote: We then align extremal chords using common supports and Darbo's fixed-point theorem and obtain a contradiction from support and convexity estimates.

backbone: Obstructed patches, residual among oscillatory-pulse perturbations, are placed near boundaries of negatively curved disks accumulating at the origin; a boundary-saddle argument excludes any isometric immersion.
quote: We construct a smooth positive-definite Riemannian metric on $`(-1,1)^2`$ that agrees with the Euclidean metric to every order at the origin, yet no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into Euclidean three-space.

backbone: If dim Sing exceeded m-1, flat scales would carry many density-Q singular centers; fitted graphs, signed excess and a height blow-up give limit measures contradicting dimension reduction.
quote: Suppose that $V$ is a stationary integral $m$-varifold in an open subset of $\R^{m+n}$ and that \[ m-1<s<\dim_{\Hh}\Sing(V). \]

backbone: Explicit torus-glued manifold from two punctured-torus products with a shear: flat-torus/CAT(0) arguments exclude nonpositive curvature, and a constructed concave-cometric neck metric is shown conjugate-point-free via index-form passage estimates.
quote: We construct a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a smooth Riemannian metric without conjugate points but admits no smooth Riemannian metric of nonpositive sectional curvature.
